Line heights

Tight lines with a line height of one. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, and then does it again to fill a second and a third line of text on a typical desktop width.

Loose lines with a line height of two. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, and then does it again to fill a second and a third line of text on a typical desktop width.

An absolute thirty pixel line height. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, and then does it again to fill a second and a third line of text.

A percentage line height of 150 percent in a sans-serif face. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, and then does it again to fill more lines.

Normal line height with a big word and a small one and some tall-line content in the middle.

Alignment and indentation

An indented first line. Subsequent lines are not indented, which is the classic paragraph style of printed books. This text goes on long enough to wrap.

A hanging indent: the first line starts at the left and the rest are pushed in by three ems, as in a bibliography entry. This text goes on long enough to wrap onto several lines.

Centred text, short.

Right-aligned text, short.

Justified text spreads the words out so that each line, except the last, fills the measure exactly. This paragraph is long enough that several lines are justified and the last one is left alone, as it should be.

Spaced letters and words, a little.

Vertical alignment

Water is H2O and area is measured in m2; a raised word, a lowered word, one six pixels up, and one half a line up inside a line.

Inline blocks: first box with a little textsecond, taller boxthird box with more text than the first one has end of line.

A bordered box with padding. Underlined text inside it.
A nested box inside the first.

  • Another item with enough text that it wraps onto a second line when the column is narrow enough.

Other elements

Written by the Typography Desk, 1 Letter Lane.
Outer quotation, long enough to wrap onto more than one line when the column is narrow.
Inner quotation, also long enough to wrap onto more than one line when the column is narrow, indented again.
Term
Definition with floated term beside it.
Longer term
A second definition that is long enough to wrap onto a second line beside the floated term.

Bold, italic, both, code, kbd, samp, var, cite, dfn, mark, strike, del, ins, small, big, tt and abbr all in one paragraph that wraps across lines.
